VSI - Knowing that Yuuichi retrieved the original key on the first day provides more context but doesn’t necessarily detract from his VSI skills. Having the original key from day one means he had a reference, but let’s not forget that the replica key was good enough to pass casual inspection and was only distinguishable upon close examination. This implies that the level of resemblance was high, even if not exact, pointing to a substantial level of skill in visual and spatial understanding. Having access to the original key doesn’t automatically make the task of creating a replica simple. If we assume yuuichi had the original key as a reference, his decision to omit the sharp edges and intricate details could have been a calculated one. Maybe he deemed these features non essential for the key to fulfill its immediate function, or perhaps he had other strategic reasons. Making such an assessment, determining which elements are critical for the replica to pass a quick scrutiny but not a detailed one, itself requires a nuanced understanding of spatial relationships and details. So even with this new information, the case for Yuuichi's strong VSI skills remains largely intact. Access to the original key might make the task somewhat easier, but the successful execution of a convincing replica still demands a considerable degree of visual and spatial ability.
